solution: Let the string have k runs of 1s. It then has k runs of 0s. Since runs have length at most 2 and there are eight 1s, k must be 4, 5, 6, 7, or 8. For a fixed k, the 1-run lengths are positive parts of 8 into k parts each at most 2, giving C(k,8-k) choices; the 0-run lengths, summing to 12, give C(k,12-k) choices. Counting labeled cyclic strings by choosing a distinguished start of a 1-run gives (20/k) times the product of these counts: there are 20 choices for its start position, and each string is counted once for each of its k 1-runs. Thus the total is Σ[k=4..8] (20/k) C(k,8-k) C(k,12-k) = 5·1·1 + 4·5·5 + (10/3)·10·10 + (20/7)·7·7 + (20/8)·1·8 = 40?
insight: A cyclic string with both digits has the same number of runs of each digit.
insight_justification: Each transition from 0 to 1 starts a 1-run and each transition from 1 to 0 ends one; around a cycle these transitions alternate, so the counts of 0-runs and 1-runs agree.
